legend: A densely cellular melanocytic proliferation composed of junctional nests of spindle and epithelioid cells that permeate the dermis. The melanocytes have uniform round or oval nuclei, conspicuous nucleoli, and pale cytoplasm. Intradermal mitotic figures are present. The melanoma metastasized to the lungs and brain, resulting in death 18 months after initial diagnosis. This tumour carried a BRAF fusion and a TERT promoter mutation.
An ulcerated epidermis with an underlying broad melanocytic neoplasm measuring 10 mm in diameter.
The melanocytes have uniform round or oval nuclei, conspicuous nucleoli, and pale cytoplasm. Intradermal mitotic figures are present, with a mitotic rate of 5 mitoses per mm<sup>2</sup>.

A tumour that developed on the thigh of an 11-year-old girl with an asymmetrical and ulcerated bulky neoplasm extending into subcutaneous fat. The tumour is 12 mm in diameter and 7 mm in thickness; no maturation is observed.

legend: Tumour that developed on the thigh of an 11-year-old girl at high magnification shows fascicles of spindle cells; the mitotic rate is 7 mitoses per mm2, and a TERT promoter mutation was confirmed. Following the initial diagnosis, the patient developed a regional clinical lymph node metastasis at 6 months and died from widespread metastases at 24 months.
A spindle cell plexiform and nested tumour, partially pigmented, invading the subcutis, with marked atypia.
